title: Daily Briefing — Monday, November 16
coverage: Covering roughly Nov 14 evening through Nov 16 morning MST, with a few flagged items from Nov 5-13 where they are still the live story. Sourcing caveat: nytimes.com is not accessible to this session's search crawler or page fetcher, so the NYT technology, science and business sections could not be checked directly; direct page fetches were also blocked (space.com failed to resolve), so items were assembled by cross-referencing multiple search summaries rather than reading primary articles. ULA has not yet identified a cause for the Vulcan failure, and reporting on the failure's location in the vehicle conflicts.

top.headline: ULA's Vulcan failed on its return-to-flight launch, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites
top.summary: The rocket suffered an anomaly roughly 10 minutes into the Nov 15 flight and lost the entire payload, ULA's first total mission failure since the Boeing-Lockheed joint venture was formed in 2006. It was the first of 38 Vulcan launches Amazon has bought, and it grounds the vehicle again just months after a February booster anomaly paused Space Force missions.

top.headline: Nvidia reports Tuesday with its CFO as interim CEO, days after Jensen Huang resigned
top.summary: Colette Kress delivers the quarter on Nov 17 while holding both the CFO and interim CEO jobs, with consensus near $109 billion in revenue. It is the first read on whether the AI capex cycle cares who runs Nvidia, and it lands the day before Anthropic prices the largest tech IPO ever attempted.

top.headline: Commerce closed the AI-chip cloud loophole and added five countries to the license list
top.summary: A BIS interim final rule now requires a license to give Chinese-headquartered entities remote access to more than 12 million aggregate TPP of compute in a data center anywhere in the world, and adds license requirements for advanced chips bound for Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil. It also formally rescinds the never-enforced Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule.

items.headline: BIS rule regulates remote access to AI chips, not just their shipment
items.summary: The interim final rule (RIN 0694-AK50) sets a license requirement for supplying more than 12,000,000 aggregate TPP of compute to entities headquartered in or controlled from China, Macau or other Country Group D:5 destinations, wherever the servers physically sit, with a 90-day window for data centers already serving those customers. Exporters get an exemption for chips going to US-headquartered companies if they file reports naming every party and the ultimate parent. Sources date the release to Nov 15 or 16; it takes effect on Federal Register publication with comments due 60 days later.

items.headline: Nvidia's first post-Huang earnings land Tuesday afternoon
items.summary: Huang resigned effective immediately on Nov 11-12 and the board named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO while appointing Harvey Jones as its first-ever chair; Kress keeps the CFO role until a permanent successor is found. Analysts expect roughly $109 billion in revenue and about $2.47 in adjusted EPS, but the questions that matter are customer commitments, the durability of the backstop-and-guarantee structures behind OpenAI's data centers, and who sets strategy from here.

items.headline: Anthropic prices Wednesday, trades Thursday under ANT, with Nvidia buying $10 billion at the IPO price
items.summary: The offering is 825 million Class A shares at $70 to $78, implying roughly $1.4 trillion, with the order book closing Tuesday and reports putting demand at six to seven times the shares on offer. Nvidia is reported to be taking $10 billion at the IPO price. Worth noting for calibration: the filing itself states no valuation, so every headline number is share count times price, and a Stocktwits poll found only 19 percent of retail respondents plan to buy.

items.headline: Reports: the administration is preparing to name AI "national champions"
items.summary: WSJ-sourced reporting says more than two dozen US AI companies, with Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic named among them, will be designated under the American AI Exports Program created by Executive Order 14320. The practical effect would be preferential treatment in government-backed export of full American AI stacks abroad. Treat this as reporting rather than policy; no designation list has been published and the rollout timing can slip.

items.headline: Materials research keeps finding that AI models need far less data than assumed
items.summary: Linköping researchers used AI to comb materials databases and surfaced MXenes that had already been synthesized but that the field had not recognized as such, a rediscovery rather than a prediction problem. Separately, Michigan Tech and UCLA reported in npj Computational Materials that materials models can discard about 90 percent of their training data with almost no accuracy loss. Both point the same direction: for physical-science models the binding constraint is data curation, not data volume.

items.headline: Vulcan anomaly destroys 40 Amazon Leo satellites in ULA's first total mission loss
items.summary: The Nov 15 return-to-flight mission failed about 10 minutes after liftoff and no satellites reached usable orbit. Northrop Grumman says its six GEM-63XL solid boosters performed as expected, and reporting disagrees on whether the fault lay in the Centaur V upper stage during its burn or in the events around separation, so treat the location as unconfirmed. Blue Origin, which supplies Vulcan's BE-4 first-stage engines, is supporting the investigation, and NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman offered agency help.

items.headline: SpaceX caught a Starship upper stage with the tower for the first time
items.summary: Ship 42 came back from about 22 hours and 14 orbits and was caught by the launch tower's arms at Starbase around 21:20 UTC on Nov 14, the first tower recovery of a Starship returning from space. Three Starlink satellites photographed the heat shield before reentry, and Musk, inspecting the tiles at the pad, said the vehicle brought back a large data set for heat-shield improvements and could refly within weeks of refurbishment. The booster's own catch was aborted the day before, so SpaceX has now demonstrated each half separately but never both on one flight.

items.headline: Electron reached 100 launches faster than any commercially developed rocket
items.summary: Rocket Lab's 100th Electron mission lifted off from Mahia, New Zealand on Nov 14 carrying iQPS's YAMATSUMI-II (QPS-SAR-19) synthetic-aperture radar satellite, which the kick stage released at roughly 575 km about 50 minutes after launch. iQPS has since confirmed first contact and antenna deployment, with first imaging still ahead. The record is about elapsed time from debut to the 100th flight, not total launches, and on that measure Electron beat Falcon 9.

items.headline: Amazon's Leo constellation now has two grounded rockets under it
items.summary: Amazon had said a second Vulcan could fly within weeks of the first; that now waits on ULA's investigation. Its other heavy-lift path, Blue Origin's New Glenn, slipped to January 2027 in a November schedule revision after the May hot-fire explosion wrecked the Launch Complex 36 tower, though CEO Dave Limp has publicly held to a 2026 attempt. For a constellation with an FCC deployment clock, the engineering problem has become a launch-supply problem.

items.headline: Aselsan says its EJDERHA microwave weapon disabled 51 drones simultaneously
items.summary: In a demonstration reported Nov 15, the high-power electromagnetic system first knocked down two tethered drones at about 1,000 meters, then disabled a swarm of 51 launched together within seconds. EJDERHA uses radar for detection and electro-optics for tracking, then directs HPEM energy at the targets' navigation, communications and command circuits rather than destroying them kinetically, which is why cost per engagement collapses against swarms. Caveat: this is the company's own announcement from its own test range, with no independent verification of conditions.

items.headline: Drones hit three civilian ships off Romania, and Bucharest wants a NATO Black Sea command
items.summary: Three vessels, including the Greek-flagged tanker Evia Petrol V, were struck near the Sulina channel on the evening of Nov 14, causing fires but no casualties, and Romanian F-16s scrambled after radar picked up an aerial target. Defense minister Stefan-Radu Oprea will press European counterparts in Brussels on Nov 17-18 for patrol aircraft and counter-drone equipment; France has temporarily forward-deployed an Atlantique 2. This is the fourth such incident since early October, and it is pushing counter-UAS from a force-protection problem to a maritime-trade problem.

items.headline: Counter-drone consolidation: Shield AI buys Echodyne, Axon takes a $1.2 billion stake in Skydio
items.summary: Both deals were announced Nov 5 and are still the live story in the sector. Shield AI is paying $4.8 billion at close plus up to $500 million in earnouts for Echodyne's MESA metamaterial electronically scanned array radars, funded by a $2.5 billion raise at a $28.8 billion valuation, with closing expected in early 2027. Axon's $1.2 billion into Skydio values it at $5.2 billion pre-money and makes Axon the exclusive US and Canada public-safety distributor. The pattern is autonomy companies buying sensing, because detection, not the interceptor, is the hard half of counter-UAS.

items.headline: FAA's Part 108 BVLOS rule is still stuck at OIRA with a Dec 7 statutory deadline
items.summary: The final rule, "Normalizing Unmanned Aircraft Systems Beyond Visual Line of Sight Operations," remains pending at the White House regulatory office, and the FAA declined to give a date at AUVSI while touting 2.2 million UTM-coordinated flights. The statutory deadline is Dec 7, 16 months after the August 2025 proposal, and the rule did not reach the White House until July 10. Until it lands, Part 107 waivers remain the only legal route to routine BVLOS operation, which is the gating item for most commercial and inspection UAV business cases.

items.headline: AIR ships its first autonomous cargo eVTOL to Florida for flight demonstrations
items.summary: Announced Nov 16, the AIR 120D is the company's first autonomous cargo variant to reach its US headquarters, where it will fly demonstrations for prospective customers. Cargo is the pragmatic entry point for eVTOL: no occupant certification basis to argue about, and payload-range economics that can be shown rather than modeled. It is a press-release milestone rather than a certification one, but the hardware moving to a US test site is the part that matters.

items.headline: Europe's next-generation EV platforms entered production within days of each other
items.summary: BMW started series production of the iX4 at Debrecen on roughly Nov 13, four months ahead of its March 2027 launch, on the Neue Klasse 800-volt architecture with cell-to-pack cylindrical cells and DC charging quoted up to 400 kW; the 612 hp iX4 M60 xDrive follows in spring 2027. Volkswagen began building the ID. Tiguan at Emden on Nov 12, merging the ID.4 and ID.5 into one model after the two sold more than 950,000 units combined. With Chattanooga ID.4 output already ended, US cars are expected to come from Emden.

items.headline: Q3 numbers show the US and European EV markets moving in opposite directions
items.summary: A quarterly tracker published Nov 16 has GM's US EV sales down 61.7 percent to 25,473 from a record 66,501 a year earlier, and Ford's Model e wholesales down about 31 percent to roughly 34,000 after F-150 Lightning production ended. Tesla outperformed the rest of the US market with deliveries off 2.1 percent, Rivian raised full-year guidance to 67,000-70,000, and Lucid delivered 3,806, down 6.7 percent. BMW Group meanwhile delivered 110,257 BEVs globally, up 7.2 percent, pulled by the Neue Klasse iX3 in Europe.

items.headline: Lamborghini's Temerario Spyder is revealed Wednesday in Los Angeles
items.summary: Teasers dropped ahead of a Nov 18 debut for the open-top Temerario. The coupe's powertrain is a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 paired with three electric motors for 907 combined horsepower, and the convertible's output has not been confirmed. The interesting engineering question is how much structural mass the roof deletion costs on a car whose hybrid system already carries a significant battery and inverter penalty.

items.headline: Las Vegas is the first street race run under the 2026 F1 rules, and it will be cold
items.summary: This weekend's round, with practice Thursday Nov 19 and the race at 8pm local Saturday Nov 21, is the first Vegas Grand Prix without DRS: the 2026 cars use active aerodynamics plus a battery-deployment Overtake Mode instead. Pirelli expects air temperatures of 10 to 15 C across three long straights and 17 corners, which makes tyre warm-up and graining, not degradation, the limiting factor. Kimi Antonelli has already clinched the drivers' title and Mercedes the constructors', so the fight is for second, where Verstappen currently sits with three wins.

engineersCorner.headline: US export control is now written in units of compute: 12,000,000 aggregate TPP
engineersCorner.body: The new BIS remote-access rule does not draw its line at a chip model or a country border but at a performance number. Total Processing Performance is roughly a chip's peak dense throughput multiplied by a bit-length factor, so summing it across a cluster gives a single scalar for "how much AI compute is sitting here." Above 12 million aggregate TPP available to a Chinese-headquartered entity, you need a license, wherever on Earth the racks are. That is on the order of a few thousand top-end datacenter GPUs, and it means a cloud contract is now an export event.

footnote: Compiled from public reporting, company and agency announcements. Figures from company statements and press reports are as reported and not independently verified.
